summary: inventory-api now runs as an enabled systemd service on node1, serves HTTP on port 8080, uses OOMScoreAdjust=-900, survives system-wide OOM pressure, and automatically recovered after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed a dependency-free inventory API and systemd unit.
Ran an isolated memory hog with OOMScoreAdjust=1000.
Verified the kernel killed the hog while inventory-api remained responsive.
Restored the temporary overcommit setting and removed stress-test artifacts.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified persistent recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is a managed, enabled, OOM-protected service
evidence.summary: Shows successful service installation, active/enabled state, port 8080 listener, runtime and configured OOMScoreAdjust=-900, and healthy API responses.

evidence.requirement: The memory hog is the process killed during OOM while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: Shows the hog launched with OOMScoreAdjust=1000; kernel logs identify its PID as the OOM victim and show SIGKILL, while inventory-api remained active at -900 and returned a healthy response.
Confirms vm.overcommit_memory returned to 0, temporary hog units were removed, and the API remained healthy.

Captures the healthy pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, boot ID change from 4b7ded33-b5e2-42c9-b7f2-bd671942a82d to 0cd8b907-1f3a-4dbc-8fdf-68131866c2f0, and post-restart service, endpoint, listener, OOM protection, artifact hashes, and current-boot startup log.
